jobDescription: A casual-dining restaurant group plans to open 12 new sites next year in retail parks and city-centre units. The New Site Opening Project Manager plans each opening from site handover to the first trading day, manages shopfitting contractors within delegated authority, coordinates kitchen equipment, utilities and licensing milestones, reports status and cost to the development committee, and leads a lessons-learned review after every opening so that the next site benefits. Shopfit packages are tendered to a framework of three contractors; the project manager can agree variations up to a delegated limit and chairs site-level dispute meetings before anything is escalated to the head of property.
requirements: Plans new-restaurant opening programmes from site handover to first trading day.
Manages shopfitting contractors, including variations and disputes, within delegated authority.
Coordinates kitchen-equipment suppliers, utility connections and licensing milestones.
Reports programme status and cost to the development committee each month.
Leads post-opening lessons-learned reviews and feeds the actions into the next programme.

evidence.text: Opening project manager at Fenwright Dining Group, April 2019 to August 2024, delivering 17 new restaurant openings across the Midlands and the North West.
Planned each opening as a 14-week programme from site handover to first trading day, covering shopfit, kitchen installation, recruitment and training.
Coordinated kitchen-equipment deliveries, utility connections and premises-licence milestones, keeping one milestone tracker per site.
Presented monthly programme status and cost reports to the development committee, with a forecast to completion for each site.
Collected feedback from the first-week operations teams after each opening and circulated a summary to the property team.

Work sample: an anonymised milestone tracker for one site, listing handover, shopfit completion, gas safety certificate, premises licence grant, staff training and first trading day with planned and actual dates.

Reference check summary: the former head of property confirmed in writing that in 2023 the candidate agreed 23 contract variations with shopfitting contractors within a £25,000 delegated limit and chaired the June 2023 dispute meeting over delayed joinery, whose minutes record the settlement the candidate agreed.
HR verification note: employment dates at Fenwright Dining Group (April 2019 to August 2024) and the job title Opening Project Manager were confirmed in writing by the employer's HR team.

propositions.text: The candidate agreed 23 contract variations with shopfitting contractors within a £25,000 delegated limit in 2023 and chaired the June 2023 dispute meeting over delayed joinery.
propositions.rationale: The reference check records the former head of property's written confirmation, the delegated limit and the minutes of the dispute meeting.

propositions.text: The candidate planned each opening as a 14-week programme from site handover to first trading day.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the programme and the work sample shows a site milestone tracker.

propositions.text: The candidate presented monthly programme status and cost reports to the development committee.

gold.expectedGap: Post-opening feedback was collected and summarised, but no lessons-learned review led by the candidate is documented.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the variation and dispute record from the reference check as supported evidence within its stated limit and year; describe the feedback summary as collection, not a led review.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate ran a structured lessons-learned review after an opening and which actions were carried into the next site.
